skill.name: find-unprofitable-products
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to find products that lose money on Google Shopping or Performance Max. Compare margins, stock, and competitor prices to understand recommendations. Submit a proposal for review only after the user confirms its details.
skill.summary: Rank products by losses after ad spend and see why Product Metrics recommends changing or keeping their priority.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The backtick, URL, and reconnaissance alerts mostly match Markdown references or routine reporting actions. The fallback query does not specify safe handling of dynamic SQL arguments, and the workflow does not require confirmation when store selection is ambiguous. No evidence of audit manipulation or credential exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The fallback CLI query does not specify how to pass dynamic SQL safely.
remediation.suggestion: Pass arguments separately without shell interpolation. Replace free-form SQL with approved read-only reporting queries and validate their parameters.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not resolve ambiguous store selection before retrieving reports or filing proposals.
remediation.suggestion: Show which Product Metrics store will be used. If more than one store matches, ask the user to choose before accessing store data.

content.user_title: Find Products That Lose Money After Ads
content.value_statement: Sales from ads can look strong even when product margins do not cover ad spend. Use Product Metrics to rank loss-making products and see the evidence behind each recommendation.
actual_capabilities: Rank unprofitable products by profit after ad spend and identify the campaigns associated with them.
Sort products for investigation by estimated weekly impact and find products that Product Metrics recommends promoting.
Explain recommendations using advertising, shopper journeys, market prices, margins, and inventory.
Compare seller offers and show weekly trends in ad cost, conversion value, and gross profit.
Check for existing proposals and submit a confirmed proposal to Priorities for approval.
limitations: Live profit by product requires the Product Metrics MCP tools. The CLI offers selected reports but cannot replace live product analysis.
Product profit is unreliable without cost prices. Profit on ad spend for Search and Demand Gen uses the account's average margin.
Only an editor or admin can file proposals after user confirmation. A proposal needs approval in Priorities before any change can take effect.
This skill does not diagnose account-wide advertising trends or switch campaign bidding to profit.

use_cases.title: Review product losses
use_cases.description: Identify which advertised products lost the most money this month and review the recommended priority for each.

use_cases.title: Explain a drop in product performance
use_cases.description: Compare weekly ad costs, conversion value, and gross profit for a product. Check which campaigns carry it and why Product Metrics recommends reducing priority.

use_cases.title: Review competitor prices
use_cases.description: Compare recent seller offers for advertised products. Separate current price gaps from quotes that may no longer be accurate.

prompt_templates.title: Find loss-making products
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store], which products lost the most money after ads in the last 30 days? Include profit after ads, profit on ad spend, and the recommendation for each.

prompt_templates.title: Explain one recommendation
prompt_templates.prompt: For [product] in [store], explain the recommendation for [period]. Compare competitor offers and their dates, and show weekly ad cost and gross profit.

prompt_templates.title: Compare losses and growth opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store] and [period], identify campaigns carrying the largest product losses. Separately list products recommended for growth and flag any missing costs or estimated margins.

prompt_templates.title: Review a priority proposal
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a proposal for approval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check existing proposals for [product] in [store]. Draft a priority reduction supported by the available evidence. Show me the exact change and rationale before submitting.

output_examples.input: Which products lost money after ads from October 1 to 30?
output: October 1 to 30: Three products lost a combined $680 after ads.
Desk Lamp was the largest loss at $320, with a profit on ad spend of 0.62.
Product Metrics recommends reducing priority. Its strongest signal was a lower competitor price.

output_examples.input: Why does Product Metrics recommend holding the Travel Mug?
output: Product Metrics recommends holding priority. Gross profit covered ad spend, but low inventory weighed against increasing priority.
The lowest reported competitor offer was $2 cheaper. The offer was recorded three days ago.

best_practices: Name the store and date range so the report covers the intended property and period.
Check cost coverage and distinguish estimated margins from product-level costs before comparing losses.
Review the recommendation and the exact proposal before confirming a change request.
anti_patterns: Treat high return on ad spend as proof that a product is profitable.
Treat an old competitor offer as a current price or change prices without merchant review.
Use break-even return on ad spend as a bidding instruction or treat a filed proposal as an applied change.

faq.question: What connection do I need?
faq.answer: Connect Product Metrics. Live product profit analysis requires its MCP tools and a store with Google Ads data and product costs.

faq.question: What does profit on ad spend measure?
faq.answer: It divides gross profit by ad spend. A value of 1 means gross profit just covers the advertising cost.

faq.question: What date range does the skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the dates you request or defaults to the last 30 days. The report states the dates used.

faq.question: What happens when a product has no cost price?
faq.answer: Its profit figure is not reliable. Check cost coverage before ranking products or acting on a recommendation.

faq.question: Is the command-line interface enough?
faq.answer: It can show selected campaign, competitor, and store reports. It cannot provide product profit based on live Google Ads results.

faq.question: Does filing a proposal change ads or prices?
faq.answer: No. Filing creates a proposal for approval in Priorities. The skill reports competitor prices but leaves pricing decisions to the merchant.
